integration.description: an outside service, as data: where a person signs in to it and where its codes are exchanged, for one reached by OAuth, the hosts its credential may be sent to, and how a page shows it. A built one is installed by the host from @yaks/connections' own seed data, and marked built; any other is a custom one, owned by the space or person that made it

name.description: what a connection names it by; the entity id is derived from it, so one name is one integration

title.description: what a person calls it, written as its maker writes it: OpenRouter, Google Calendar

tagline.description: one line saying what it is, written for a person

logo.description: its mark, as an SVG document; a page draws it as an image, never as markup

authorize.description: where a person grants access, for an integration reached by OAuth

token.description: where codes and refresh tokens are exchanged; an integration with none is a pasted key

scopes.description: what a connection asks for when nothing narrower was needed

params.description: extra parameters the authorize link carries, such as Google's access_type

auth.description: how the client authenticates at the token endpoint (default basic)

refresh_encoding.description: how the token endpoint receives refresh grants (default form)

answers.description: what the token endpoint answers: tokens (the default), or an API key, as OpenRouter's PKCE exchange does

resource.description: the resource a grant is for (RFC 8707), sent with the sign-in link and every exchange, as an MCP server asks

issuer.description: the issuer every sign-in return must name (RFC 9207), for a service that says it names one

client.description: the OAuth client it signs in as, by name: kept once as the secret `oauth_client <name>`, and shared by every integration naming it. Only a built integration signs in as a client a built one names

client_id.description: a public OAuth client's id, shipped with a built integration

hosts.description: the API hosts a connection's credential may be sent to, and no others

signature.description: how the service signs the webhooks it sends (@yaks/hook's Scheme)

testing.description: still in the service's testing mode, where only the people it lists may sign in: a page offers it only where asked to by name

built.description: installed by the host from @yaks/connections' own seed data. Only the host writes it, so no space can mark an integration built or sign in as a built one's client

userinfo.description: OpenID endpoint naming the signed-in account when the token answer has no id_token

instructions.description: how a person gets the credential, in markdown, written for them and for the agent helping them: where to sign up, which page issues the key, what to paste. Shown beside every connection it is needed for

owner.description: the space or person that made a custom integration: only its owner may change the integration's title, tagline, site or instructions, and nobody may change its hosts. A built integration has none, and is the host's

by.description: who listed it, kept as history when that entity is deleted

via.description: what the write was made through: the session or client it came in on

listed.description: a custom integration shown in the integration directory, which anyone may read and add to a space of their own, apart from any app: its owner's act, and taking the mark off takes it out. Every built integration is shown without it

connection.description: one link between a space or a person and an outside service, through an integration. The entity is also the secret its credential is kept as: the graph holds the handle, the vault the key or the tokens

integration.description: the integration it goes through, by name

owner.description: the space or the person it belongs to; it is deleted with them, and its credential with it

account.description: which account at the outside service, as the person would recognize it

scopes.description: what it was granted, or what the app that needs it asked for

status.description: needed: no credential yet; connected: one is kept; broken: the service refused it

anyone.description: anyone may call out through it, signed in or not, as a public widget does; otherwise only a caller holding a level on the app

each.description: each person who uses the app connects their own, and only the person who owns the connection calls out through it: set on the app's ask, the needed connection its space holds, and on the link to every person's own

binding.description: the name the app's code reads it by, env.NAME in a worker: the sentinel for its credential, or the credential itself where the link is direct

direct.description: the app's code is handed the credential itself rather than a sentinel, for a key it must transform before sending (a signature, Basic auth); only a pasted key may be

cap.description: the most calls a month that may go out through it (@yaks/egress `calls`); past it the egress refuses them until the month turns. None is no limit. Only the host sets it, never the app it caps

lends.description: on an app's link to a connection its own space keeps: the connection is lent to every copy installed from the app, which borrows it rather than asking for its own, and this is the cap each copy's link borrows it under, in calls a month. None lends it to no copy. The space owner's act, and only a sentinel every caller shares is lent: never a direct key, nor a link where each person connects their own

lender.description: on a copy's link to a connection it borrows rather than holds: the app whose lend it borrows it through. The copy's space connects a key of its own to stop borrowing, and the lender stops lending to it, either way leaving the lender's connection as it was. Only the host writes it, when the copy is installed or updated

uses.description: the relation on a link: this app calls out through that connection

connection_need.title: Say an app needs a connection
connection_need.description: Say that an app needs an outside service: an integration by name, and the scopes it asks for. It makes a connection with no credential, owned by a space or a person, which shows them what to connect; no key or token ever passes through this tool. For a service with no built integration, name it and give the hosts its key may be sent to, and a custom integration is made for it, owned by the asking space; give it instructions too, markdown for a person and their agent saying how to get the key (where to sign up, which page issues it, what to paste), and a title, tagline and site. Its owner asking again with any of those changes them; its hosts never change. With each, every person who uses the app connects their own instead, and the owner connects nothing. An app that already uses a connection through that integration is answered with it. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components written, followed by the integration the connection goes through, its instructions among it, to walk the person through getting the key.

app.description: the app that needs it, by id or name

owner.description: the space or person who will connect it, by id or name

scopes.description: what the app asks for; omit for the integration's own

hosts.description: for a custom key only: the hosts it may be sent to

each.description: each person who uses the app connects their own account, rather than the owner connecting one for everyone. The host draws the Connect button for them, each person's connection shows in their own dashboard, and only they call out through it

binding.description: the name the app's code reads it by (env.NAME); omit for the integration's name in capitals

direct.description: hand the app's code the key itself rather than a sentinel, for a key it must sign with; only for a pasted key

instructions.description: for a custom integration: how a person gets its key, in markdown, written for them and the agent helping them

title.description: for a custom integration: what a person calls the service, as its maker writes it

tagline.description: for a custom integration: one line saying what the service is

site.description: for a custom integration: the service's https address on the web

connection_list.title: List connections
connection_list.description: The connections a space or a person owns, each with its integration, account, scopes and status (needed, connected or broken), the links from each app that uses one, and the integrations they go through, with each one's instructions for getting its key. A handle is shown where a credential is kept; the credential itself never is. Returns bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and component fields.

owner.description: the space or person, by id or name

integration_install.description: install the integrations this package builds whenever a process starts working the effects; a graph already holding them as shipped is read once and written nothing
